sources.title: Perseverance Rover Location Map
sources.instrument: HiRISE (MRO) high-resolution basemap; Mars Express HRSC regional basemap
sources.acquisitionDate: Traverse represented by map; page describes latest rover location, accessed 2026-11-12
sources.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech; basemap imagery credited to NASA/HiRISE and ESA/DLR/FU Berlin (HRSC)
sources.limitations: Page text documents the map layers and drive-endpoint/sol symbology but does not expose machine-readable traverse coordinates. Color processing is applied; not a substitute for source rasters or coordinate-bearing mission data.

sources.title: Mars Rock Samples
sources.instrument: Perseverance sampling system; sample site investigations used rover science instruments
sources.productId: NASA public sample inventory; links to Mars 2020 Sample Dossier PDFs
sources.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech; sample dossier archive at NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node
sources.limitations: Inventory identifies sampling-location names and sample metadata, not site latitude/longitude. Do not infer exact coordinates or use the sample names as the identity of a hypothetical waypoint.

sources.title: PDS Geosciences Node: Mars 2020 Mission Data and Services
sources.instrument: Mission archive index; links to instrument bundles, sample dossier, Three Forks depot, and rover PLACES bundle
sources.productId: Mars 2020 PDS Release 16 (sols 1740–1859; archive page dated 2026-08-11)
sources.attribution: NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node / Washington University in St. Louis
sources.limitations: This is an archive index, not itself a traverse geometry file. It points to the Sample Dossier Bundle and PLACES bundle; their presence does not establish that either provides a ready-to-use geographic traverse GeoJSON.

sources.title: Mars 2020 Rover PLACES Bundle
sources.instrument: Rover localization and mechanism-position archive (PLACES; operational position/localization data, not a science instrument)
sources.attribution: NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node / Washington University in St. Louis; Mars 2020 mission
sources.limitations: Official archive documents rover localizations and mechanism positions and links to product collections and SIS; this index does not promise GeoJSON. Coordinate frames, localization fields, product structure, and suitability for a surface traverse must be checked against the SIS and release notes before extracting or interpreting route points.
